messages:
Anya: Quick q — our streaming endpoints currently set `Cache-Control: no-cache` which prevents proxy caching, but we still want to surface whether a prompt/prefix was served from the prompt cache. Do we prefer a response header, a JSON field at the end of the stream, or both? cc @Matt @Ashok

Matt: My vote is a header + a stable response field for non-streaming. For streaming we can emit a final sentinel event with a small JSON payload that includes `cache_hit` and `cache_key_meta`. Keep it opt-in via a query param so clients that care can opt in.

Ashok: Agree on opt-in. Two compatibility points: 1) existing clients expect no extra events in stream; 2) reverse proxies may strip non-standard headers. So header alone is brittle.

Lina: +1 to header+body. Suggest header be minimal `x-rw-cache: hit|miss|stale` and the final JSON provide `cache_hit: true/false`, `cache_ttl_s`, and `cache_key_v1` if present. Example for non-streaming:```HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: private, max-age=0, must-revalidate
x-rw-cache: hit
Content-Type: application/json

{ "output": "...", "cache_hit": true, "cache_ttl_s": 300, "cache_key_v1": "pfx:abcd1234" }```

Ben: Small worry: some customers rely on `Cache-Control` semantics for CDN routing. If we add `x-rw-cache: stale` when serving a stale-but-revalidate entry, clients may think data is fresh. We should document the combined semantics: `x-rw-cache` describes origin cache state, `Cache-Control` continues to guide proxies.

Anya: Good call. So concretely: - Keep `Cache-Control` unchanged by default. - Add `x-rw-cache: hit|miss|stale` header. - Add opt-in param `?cache_signals=1` that, when set, appends a final JSON chunk for streaming with fields: `cache_hit`, `cache_status`, `cache_key_v1` (if not sensitive), `served_from` (host id).

Ashok: For privacy we should never expose raw prompt text or user-identifying keys. `cache_key_v1` should be a safe hash (prefix-only) or omitted. Also add a flag `cache_key_redacted: true` when redacted.

Matt: Implementation notes: runtime can set header early for non-stream responses. For streaming, we will emit the final chunk as a newline-delimited JSON event with an event type, e.g.:```event: cache_signal
data: {"cache_hit":true,"cache_status":"hit","cache_ttl_s":300,"cache_key_v1":"pfx:abcd...","cache_key_redacted":false}```Clients that don't parse NDJSON will ignore it. We need SDK support to unwrap that last event.

Lina: How about backcompat: some users introspect `x-cache` today. We should add `x-rw-cache` but also set `x-cache` for a transitional period with same value to avoid surprises. Add a deprecation header `x-rw-cache-v2: true` in responses during the migration window.

Ben: I'll draft a quick RFC with the header names, streaming event schema, and examples for our docs + SDKs. Action item: @Ashok can you confirm we won't leak keys, and @Matt can you scope SDK change for the streaming client?

Ashok: I'll validate hash-only key strategy. If we decide to include `served_from`, we'll make it node id only (no AZ/cust data).

Matt: SDK change: add `onCacheSignal` callback to streaming client and set `cache_signals` opt-in default to false. I can PR next week.

sre-bot: deploy noticed a canary for "prefix-cache-signals" rolled out to 10% at 2025-09-09T14:10:03Z — no errors reported.

Anya: Thanks all — Ben, ping when RFC is up and I'll add examples to the API reference. Small follow-up: should we include `x-rw-cache` for 204/empty responses too? I think yes for uniformity.

Ben: Agreed. I'll include that. Will share RFC link here when ready. :+1:
